prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create a square watercolor storyboard, ideally 1536×1536, exactly TWO columns by THREE rows, six independent 3:2 LANDSCAPE panels in row-major order. Equal cells with a narrow clear ivory paper gap, no borders, labels or frames; no scene crosses a cell boundary. Keep the full primary subject inside the central 82% of each cell.
MEDIUM ONLY is shared: sophisticated adult editorial watercolor on warm ivory cold-pressed paper, transparent layered washes, expressive pencil contours, irregular pigment edges softly dissolving into unpainted paper. Sage, terracotta, lavender, soft ochre with scene-appropriate blues and greens. Loose believable anatomy and gestures, not photographic, not 3D, not cartoon. Warm and adult, but do NOT impose golden sunshine or a cozy room on every setting.
Each panel illustrates the SPECIFIC QUESTION supplied, not merely the topic. Make the action or idea readable without a caption. Change the subject, action, setting, scale or viewpoint substantially for every panel. A close crop of a prop from the preceding scene is not a new concept. Use the concrete directions below, no decorative filler or invented extra scenes.
Fictional adults and natural hands/gestures are welcome where specified; use candid back/side/over-shoulder views or crop naturally above the chin, never blank faceless heads. No idealized romance, no default gender roles, no recognizable real person. Adults of ordinary appearance, varied skin tones. These are fictional examples, not reconstructions of a user's memories. Emotion can be mixed; do not visually assert reconciliation or a promised outcome.
STRICTLY NO cups, mugs, drinking glasses, plates, cutlery, kettles, table settings, flower vases, decorative bouquets, hearts, rings, floating icons, puzzle metaphors, UI, captions, letters, numbers, handwriting, logos or watermarks. No café, Tuscan room or wicker furniture unless expressly requested. Book pages, maps, tickets and screens must have no readable writing. Do not fill unrelated panels with the same furniture, fabric or object.
STORY S12: Our first try
PANEL 1
Question context (do not render as text): What new thing would you like to try with me?
Paint: At an outdoor rental rack, two fictional adults pause curiously beside a simple two-person kayak, one points toward the water and the other leans in to look; the moment of choosing something new, not already succeeding. Unbranded equipment, empty river beyond.
PANEL 2
Question context (do not render as text): Picture us trying that new thing. What part would you look forward to?
Paint: Two first-time adult kayakers push off from a low jetty, paddles held cautiously and a small bright splash at the bow; over-shoulder view toward the open calm water, anticipation of the first few minutes. Wear simple life jackets.
PANEL 3
Question context (do not render as text): If our first try went badly, what could make it fun anyway?
Paint: A harmless beginner kayak wobble in very shallow calm water beside the jetty: both adults remain seated safely in life jackets, one paddle splashes its own partner and both laugh, expressive candid gestures. Funny imperfect attempt, no capsizing or peril.
PANEL 4
Question context (do not render as text): When you try something new, what kind of help do you like from me?
Paint: On dry riverbank, one adult offers a paddle flat across open palms while the other practices their own grip; supportive help offered rather than hands correcting their body. Medium-close view of the distinct gesture, kayak soft in background.
PANEL 5
Question context (do not render as text): What would a small first try of our idea look like?
Paint: Wide view of the kayak making one tiny practice loop just beside the safe jetty, two cautious adults paddling together in calm shallow water, the bank visibly close. A small achievable first try, no distant expedition or success trophy.
PANEL 6
Question context (do not render as text): If you like, keep our idea for a first try. It can stay an idea.
Paint: A single paddle and two plain life jackets hanging on the rental rack beside the calm river, kayak resting on the bank; the option remains available without anyone having to set out. Spare hopeful watercolor scene.
